title: I made "Game of Life" in a minute with AI Game Developer
author: BAIZOR
selftext:
I built Conway’s Game of Life in Unity in about 60 seconds using my free tool: AI Game Developer — an AI-assisted workflow that helps generate/modify code, iterate fast, and keep everything inside a real Unity project.

[AI Game Developer at GitHub](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP)

 What it does
- Creates a working Game of Life implementation in Unity (grid, update loop, rules, visualization)
- Helps iterate quickly (change grid size, speed, colors, patterns, input controls, etc.)
- Keeps changes project-friendly (readable code + easy to tweak)

Feedback
I am the creator of AI Game Developer, I am glad to hear your feedback. Thanks!

comments.author: CulturalFig1237
comments.body: This feels like a good example of AI as an accelerator instead of a replacement. If it helps you iterate without breaking the project structure, that is genuinely useful.

replies.author: BAIZOR
replies.body: Absolutely. It helps in daily routine during game development. Because it can fix problem for you or to make a feature for you. Basically it brings the power of high-end agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and others into Unity Editor.

comments.author: splashtriplered
comments.body: your simulation is bugged btw, thats a project that is very easy to do without AI...

replies.author: BAIZOR
replies.body: This a bit updated version. It has more pixel colors with different properties. Such as coal, grass, fire, water etc. Grass grows if touches water. Fire burns wood and grass and creates coal. Stone can block fire and grass growing. Sand may fall down as well as water.

replies.author: mewhenidothefunni
replies.body: but these are black and white?

replies.author: BAIZOR
replies.body: I did not use others for the demo, only Life cell. They also burn and turn into coal if contact with fire cell
